entries.title: uninstall keeps your own section after the policy
entries.summary: uninstall strips the Code Exploration Policy and nothing after it: a section of yours headed # or ### right after the policy used to go with it. The policy block now starts at a real heading, never a fenced example of one or a heading that only mentions it, and a byte-order mark no longer hides it. Installers no longer skip a file that only mentions the policy in a sentence.

entries.title: a schema's dead-code advice follows the right evidence
entries.summary: find_dead_code and check_delete_safe never certify a .xsd or .wsdl with no importer, and the advice they give depends on whether the repository looks like .NET. A Razor or Blazor tree now counts as .NET, and a bare .fs file no longer does, so a GLSL shader no longer makes a Maven repository read as .NET. Every schema stays capped either way; only the advice changes.

entries.title: seven import forms record the names they import
entries.summary: A PHP group use, a Kotlin `as` import, a Scala selector, a Haskell import list, a Dart `show`, a destructuring `require` and a Python `import` continued by a backslash each recorded no names, or no edge, so find_references answered 0 for the names they import. Each now records them, and a statement that is not whole records what it did before. The parser generation moves, so an existing index re-reads these files once.

entries.title: indexing a drive root keeps its files, and LSP enrichment runs no Rust build scripts
entries.summary: A folder prefix built as folder + separator doubled the separator for a filesystem root, so indexing a drive root kept no files and a root .gitignore would not have applied; every prefix now comes from one rule. With LSP enrichment on, rust-analyzer starts with build scripts, procedural macros and check-on-save off, so it no longer runs a Rust project's build.rs by default. The 1.50.0 branch delta layers never ran, and the record now says so; the index follows the checked-out tree, as it always has.
